title: Alfred Adler's birth chart
metaDescription: Alfred Adler's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 18.5° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a sextile: Mars and Saturn within 0.1°, drive wired to structure. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 18.5° Aquarius: the second decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Mercury. A air sign, read here in its second face.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 9.2° Aquarius, Venus was at 12.5° Pisces, Mars was at 25.8° Aquarius. Read together: a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Mars and Saturn: 0.1° from an exact sextile. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional. Behind it, Venus sextile Jupiter at 0.3°, and the Sun sextile Neptune at 1.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has two entries for this chart. The Sun in Aquarius at 18.5° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Pisces at 12.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: air 3, water 2, earth 2, fire 2 across the elements, and fixed 5, mutable 2, cardinal 2 across the modalities. Air signs carry exchange in the scheme — comparison, argument, the sentence that makes the situation legible. Mercury, Venus and Uranus were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day at the birthplace, travelling 11.9° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
